§6Oil Tar§f

§aFive variants, one purpose: tanks, dye, and coking. Pick whichever you can make cheapest.§f

Oil Tar is a sticky petroleum product with five interchangeable variants: §bOil Tar§f, §bCrack Oil Tar§f, §bCoal Tar§f, §bWood Tar§f, and §bParaffin Wax§f.

§6Production§f:
§b• Oil Tar§f: Solidify Crude Oil, Bitumen, or Heavy Oil in the §bIndustrial Solidification Machine§f.
§b• Crack Oil Tar§f: Byproduct from refining §bCracked Oil§f (replaces sulfur).
§b• Coal Tar§f: Solidify §bCoal Oil§f from the §bIndustrial Liquefaction Machine§f. Easiest to mass-produce.
§b• Wood Tar§f: Solidify §bWood Oil§f. Cannot be acidized into Chlorinated Petroleum Wax.
§b• Paraffin Wax§f: Solidify §bEngine Lubricant§f. Combines with §bChlorine Gas§f in the §bAcidizer§f.

§6Uses§f:
§b• Black Dye§f: Substitute in crafting recipes.
§b• Fluid Tanks§f: Required for §bSteel Barrels§f, §bUniversal Fluid Tanks§f, and the §bBAT-9000§f.
§b• Coke§f: Wood Tar in the §bCombination Oven§f → §bCoke§f.

§ePS:§f The §bIndustrial Liquefaction Machine§f needs tar to craft, so start with §bCrude Oil§f solidification for your first batch.
